A $17,970,734 capitalization — a $12,840,000 senior first mortgage at 8.79% floating, interest-only for a three-year term, a $770,000 acquisition loan, and $4,360,734 of preferred equity — refinancing the existing loan, funding a full renovation, and acquiring the adjacent waterfront parcel on a 58-key resort in Talbot County, Maryland.

Senior Director · Exclusive Capital Advisor
wylder Tilghman Island
October 7, 2026 · Tilghman Island, MD

Summary of the capitalization.

Marcus & Millichap Capital Corporation is placing a $17,970,734 capitalization for Wylder Hotel Tilghman Island: a senior first mortgage, an acquisition loan on the adjacent waterfront parcel and a preferred equity tranche sized so that no common equity is required at close. The proceeds retire the existing loan, fund a full renovation of all 57 guest rooms, buy and renovate the adjacent residence and marina, and establish twelve months of debt service and preferred current-pay reserves.

Wylder Hotel Tilghman Island · Senior Debt & Preferred Equity MMCC · The TRANCHE Group02

A 57-key waterfront resort on 8.10 acres, with an adjacent parcel under contract.

Wylder Hotel Tilghman Island sits on Tilghman Island in Talbot County, Maryland, between the Chesapeake Bay and the Choptank River — an 8.10-acre waterfront parcel with 1,100 feet of water frontage, a marina, pool, restaurant and boat bar. Operated under the Wylder Hotels brand, the property is mid-repositioning, with a Small Luxury Hotels affiliation planned for Year 2. The adjacent parcel at 21441 Dogwood Cove — three acres, a four-bedroom residence and 24 boat slips — is under contract and funded in this capitalization; see page 5.

Acquired by 21551 Tilghman Investors LLC, the entity that owns the hotel, so the parcel comes into the existing collateral rather than a separate venture. The 45-day closing period runs in parallel with the senior loan closing.

The parcel sits at 21441 Dogwood Cove, Tilghman, Talbot County, Maryland.

What It Adds
Boat slips24
Land±3 acres
Residence4 bedrooms
Keys1 · whole-home suite
Site on completion±11.1 acres
Marina slips on completion47

The residence becomes a whole-home suite, a product the hotel cannot offer today, and is counted as the 58th key. Its 24 slips take the marina from 23 slips today to 47 on completion.

It is underwritten conservatively — a $1,500 nightly rate at 35% occupancy, or $191,625 of annual revenue from stabilization, against a $1,400,000 all-in cost.

Why It Matters

The parcel was part of the hotel until it was separated and sold to a third party during a bankruptcy roughly ten years ago. Acquiring it reassembles the original assemblage and takes the last private parcel between the hotel and its waterfront off the market.

It is funded by a $770,000 acquisition loan at 70% of purchase price, with the balance and the renovation carried inside the capitalization. Debt service of $72,955 a year is included in every coverage figure in this package.

The expanded marina and the whole-home suite are the two revenue sources that have never existed at the property. Together with the seven keys returned to service, they account for $976,214 of revenue at stabilization that no historical period contains.

Ownership and operating structure.

The property is owned by 21551 Tilghman Investors LLC, led by principal John Flannigan, and operated under the Wylder Hotels brand through affiliate Wylder Eastern Shore Management, LLC — controlling day-to-day operations and the renovation, with a Small Luxury Hotels affiliation planned for Year 2.

Structure and Alignment
01Owner-operated, no third-party manager — Day-to-day operations are run by an affiliate of ownership. There is no third-party management agreement to terminate or subordinate, no comfort letter to negotiate and no split incentive between owner and operator.
02Continuous ownership since 2017 — The sponsor has owned and operated the hotel under the Wylder brand through the pandemic cycle and the current repositioning, investing a further $642,693 of capital between 2021 and 2025.
03Single-asset ownership entity — 21551 Tilghman Investors LLC holds this property and, on closing, the adjacent Dogwood Cove parcel — and no other operating assets — keeping the collateral and its cash flow ring-fenced.
04Two-property brand platform — Revenue management, distribution, design and procurement are shared across Wylder Hotels in Maryland and New York, giving a 57-key asset reach it could not support standing alone.

Operating statements are produced monthly at the property level and are the basis for the historical figures in this package. Financial reporting, revenue management and the renovation are handled in-house.

Business plan and capital improvement program.

Capital Improvement Program $3.3M · $56,948 / key · Sep 2026 – Apr 2027
01
Guest room renovation
Full renovation of all 57 guest rooms at $25,000 per key. Four out-of-service keys are returned and three added in the back house, taking the hotel from 50 to 57 — 12.3% more sellable inventory that has never produced revenue.
$1.43M
02
Additional revenue sources
The marina — 23 slips today, 47 with the Dogwood Cove acquisition, rebuilt for $250,000 — carries almost no operating overhead and contributes roughly $341,000 a year of departmental profit at stabilization, on revenue the property has never captured. A reconfigured boat bar and rebuilt three-bedroom house add further sources, and the adjacent Dogwood Cove residence adds a whole-home suite.
$0.85M
03
Brand affiliation
Operation under the Wylder Hotels brand, with a planned Small Luxury Hotels affiliation in Year 2 distributed through Hilton channels.
SLH · Yr 2

Exterior and interior improvements, contingency and professional fees complete the $3,003,000 hotel program, equal to $52,684 per key across the 57 hotel keys. With $300,000 for the Dogwood Cove residence the total capital program is $3,303,000, or $56,948 per key on 58 keys. The program is funded from the capitalization set out on page 18, together with $300,000 for the Dogwood Cove residence.

The Model Room Is Built

The guest-room specification is complete and can be inspected on site. Finishes, casegoods, lighting, soft goods and bath are installed. The $25,000 per key in the budget is priced against a room that exists rather than a drawing, which takes design and specification risk out of the remaining keys and gives the schedule a known unit cost to roll out.

Small Luxury Hotels affiliation and distribution.

Why the Affiliation Matters
Hilton Distribution

SLH member hotels are bookable directly through Hilton.com, the Hilton app and Hilton Honors. The affiliation places the property inside Hilton’s reservation and loyalty system rather than leaving it dependent on direct booking and third-party channels, which is the mechanism behind the projected occupancy and rate gain.

An Established Relationship

The sponsor already operates within SLH. Wylder Windham, the sister hotel in the Catskills, is an SLH member and was the first in that market. The application here is an extension of a working relationship rather than a first approach.

American Express Fine Hotels & Resorts

Wylder Windham carries the American Express Fine Hotels & Resorts designation, reached through the SLH platform. The same designation is the plan at Tilghman Island, adding a high-rate corporate and affluent leisure channel on completion.

Affiliation is targeted on completion of the renovation and remains subject to application, inspection, board approval and an executed brand affiliate agreement.

The marina is rebuilt and expanded for $250,000 inside the capital plan and carries almost no operating overhead; the model loads it with a 5% direct cost, leaving $341,332 of departmental profit at stabilization. Four out-of-service keys returned and three added in the back house lift sellable inventory 12.3%. The Dogwood Cove house is underwritten at a $1,500 nightly rate and 35% occupancy as a whole-home suite. Food and beverage is a larger share of revenue than the resort segment because of the crab shack, bar and event space against only 57 keys, but restaurant revenue per seat is 20% below the comparable average and event revenue per occupied room is close to the $180 the property itself achieved in 2025.

Food and beverage cost of 60.0% against a 72.0% segment figure reflects a limited-menu seasonal outlet and event catering rather than a three-meal restaurant. Credit card commissions of 2.9% are carried in undistributed expenses and have no separate segment comparator.

What the Market Trend Supports

Market supply has been unchanged at approximately 404 rooms since 2022, while demand has grown in each of the last two years and reached a ten-year high of 84,017 room nights in 2025. Trailing twelve-month demand through March 2026 is running 5.6% ahead of the prior period. Market RevPAR has compounded at 6.0% a year since 2019 and stands at a record $199. The projections adopt none of this growth: rate and occupancy for the competitive market are held flat at 2025 levels throughout, so the entire RevPAR gain in the plan is attributed to the renovation, the seven added keys, the expanded marina, the adjacent parcel and the brand affiliation.

Of the $17,970,734 total capitalization, $11,814,782 retires the existing loan and buys the adjacent parcel, $3,303,000 funds capital improvements, $2,137,664 funds reserves and working capital, and $715,288 covers financing costs. No common equity is required at close and no proceeds are distributed to the sponsor.

Cost Basis

Total project cost basis of $17,970,734 ($309,840 per key on 58 keys) against a $12,840,000 senior loan and $13,610,000 of total debt. Basis above the senior loan is $5,130,734, or 28.5% of cost.

Interest-Only Structure

Three-year term, interest-only for the full term at an 8.79% floating all-in rate. Combined annual debt service is $1,201,591 and is reserved for twelve months at close. A permanent takeout at 6.50% over a 30-year amortization would carry $973,890, covered 2.74x at stabilization.

Preferred Equity

The $4,360,734 preferred tranche is subordinate to both loans, pays 10% current and accrues 7%, and is sized cash-neutral so the sponsor contributes no new common equity. Twelve months of current pay is reserved from proceeds.

Sponsor Support

Completion and cost-overrun guaranty, full carry guaranty through renovation and stabilization, recourse carve-outs and environmental indemnity, and a $10,000,000 minimum net-worth covenant on the guarantor.

The Position

The as-is estimate of $368,966 per key sits below the average of both comparable sets — the East Coast waterfront sales and the eight resort trades closed since January 2025 — and between the median and the average of the more recent set.

The stabilized estimate of $508,621 per key sits below the two highest recent resort trades, at $741,000 and $893,000 per key, and is reached only after a $3,303,000 capital program, the adjacent-parcel acquisition and brand affiliation.

Total project cost basis of $309,840 per key remains below the as-is estimate, and the senior loan attaches at $221,379 per key.

The Tilghman Island Inn is the nearest transaction and is reported under contract at $5,200,000. It is a 20-key upper-midscale property configured as condominium units on five acres, with 1,800 SF of meeting space and seven slips. It carries neither the key count, the two food and beverage outlets, the marina, the 3,722 SF of event space nor the income base of the subject, and it establishes small-inn pricing on the island rather than resort pricing.

What the Local Set Does Establish

The Tidewater Inn, an 89-key full-service hotel in Easton, is expected to be brought to market in 2026 and reported 2025 occupancy of 48% at a $238 average rate on approximately $950,000 of net operating income. It is the only property in the local set operating at institutional scale, and it does so at a rate 43% below the subject’s $415 stabilized projection and without waterfront, marina or resort positioning. The Robert Morris Inn in Oxford, 16 keys, traded at $200,000 per key in 2024 and is now closed and back on the market at a lower asking price. The local evidence brackets the subject rather than pricing it: small and partly distressed inns below, and a single larger property in a materially different product tier.

The eight resort transactions at left average 44 keys, closely matching the subject at 57 hotel keys, and support a per-key range of $266,000 to $893,000 with a median of $332,000. The estimated as-is value of $368,966 per key sits between that median and the average.
